This explains why chronic burnout feels physically exhausting, even without heavy activity. Researchers note that repeated sympathetic activation elevates blood pressure, disrupts metabolism, and weakens immunity. Interestingly, mild stress can sharpen focus, but prolonged activation creates the opposite effect: cognitive fog and emotional numbness. The interplay between ANS dysfunction and hormonal imbalance magnifies the psychological toll of relentless work, social pressure, or environmental threat. Even ancient survival stressors didn’t impose 24/7 sympathetic activation; our bodies are trapped in a constant alert state. Recognizing this mechanism reframes burnout as a multi-systemic physiological event.
